claim: Generated prose (CLAUDE.md, rule files) compiles from the graph wherever there is an oracle to diff against, and its freshness is enforced structurally in CI - a gate fails on drift - not procedurally, per cb:b386. Hand-written prose is reserved for a distinct audience, the front-door README, and must never freeze graph-derived facts such as counts or lists, which drift; it points at the live source instead.

evidence.detail: Refines CB-RESTRUCTURE-HANDOFF.md §2.3: the original 'hand-written exception ~nil' was revised this session - the front-door README stays hand-written (distinct audience: a GitHub reader who cannot query the graph), with the discipline narrowed to 'no frozen derived facts' rather than 'no hand-written prose'. Realized by b042 (compiled CLAUDE.md) + the CI freshness gate.

Second conforming instance of the hand-written-prose case: amieval/CLAUDE.md, the tree-root session-start router created 2026-06-22 as the agent-behavior:a165 surfacing fix. It is hand-written by design - it routes to the graph (delegates the session-start ritual to composable-beliefs/CLAUDE.md, names the desk query, points at collections.json as the live collection map) rather than embedding directive or schema content, so the cb:b386 drift risk does not apply. Extends this principle's hand-written audience beyond the front-door README to the agent-facing tree root, holding the no-frozen-graph-derived-lists / point-at-live-source discipline (the repos enumeration was dropped for exactly this reason). Settled at the operator's request, replacing an earlier in-file note that mis-cited cb:b543 (the global ~/.claude cross-project graph) as a compilation blocker.
